applicable_when: This kernel is a tensor layout transpose: input has stride (4032000,1,32000,128) and output has stride (4032000,31500,250,1). The load index y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1 strides by 128 elements (512 bytes) in the x-dimension, making consecutive threads in the x-warp access non-contiguous memory. This causes 0% L1 hit rate and drives L2 to 96.9% utilization. The dominant stall (58.9% of cycles) is L1TEX scoreboard latency (44.2 cycles avg). Adding tl.max_contiguous/tl.multiple_of hints on the load pointer tells the compiler the access is contiguous within a tile, enabling 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads. Simultaneously, @triton.autotune explores YBLOCK/XBLOCK combinations to maximize L2 cache reuse across the strided dimension.
